title: Sale’s Brigade in Afghanistan (Illustrated)
subtitle: With an Account of the Seizure and Defence of Jellalabad
author: george-robert-gleig

description.short: In October 1841 a single brigade marched east from Kabul under orders for India. It forced the Khoord Cabul pass with its commander wounded in the ankle, fought rear-guard actions through Tezeen and Gundamuck, and in November occupied the broken walls of Jellalabad. Behind it the British army at Kabul was destroyed on its retreat. The 13th Light Infantry, the 35th Bengal Native Infantry, Broadfoot's sappers, Abbott's guns, a squadron of Bengal cavalry and a rassalah of Shah Shuja's horse rebuilt the town's defences, lost them to an earthquake on 19 February 1842, rebuilt them again, and on 7 April marched out and broke Akbar Khan's besieging army in the open field, nine days before the relief arrived.
description.long: Complete text of the 1846 first edition in gently refreshed English Sixteen plates of 1839 to 1879, with portraits of Sale and Gleig Publisher’s note and afterword, author and commander profiles Timeline, glossary, dramatis personae and order of battle Note on this edition listing every correction to the 1846 printing In October 1841 a single brigade marched east from Kabul under orders for India. It forced the Khoord Cabul pass with its commander wounded in the ankle, fought rear-guard actions through Tezeen and Gundamuck, and in November occupied the broken walls of Jellalabad. Behind it the British army at Kabul was destroyed on its retreat. The 13th Light Infantry, the 35th Bengal Native Infantry, Broadfoot's sappers, Abbott's guns, a squadron of Bengal cavalry and a rassalah of Shah Shuja's horse rebuilt the town's defences, lost them to an earthquake on 19 February 1842, rebuilt them again, and on 7 April marched out and broke Akbar Khan's besieging army in the open field, nine days before the relief arrived. George Robert Gleig, a Peninsula officer turned clergyman, wrote the brigade's history in 1846 from its officers' journals and the Orderly Books of the 13th. His judgement on the war is severe. His account of the garrison is exact. This AETERNUS edition follows the first edition of John Murray, London, 1846, in gently modernised English: long sentences divided, punctuation brought into present use, Gleig's spellings of names kept. Eighteen images have been added, among them the 1845 mezzotint of Sir Robert Sale and the engraved portrait of Gleig; the first edition had none. A Publisher's Note, an Afterword, an account of the author and a Glossary complete the volume. GREEN SERIES · AETERNUS
